chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ibn Bukayr, from Ubayd ibn Zurara, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

Regarding a man who performed the Obligatory Tawaaf and did not pray the two cycles until he performed Tawaaf between As-Safa and Al-Marwa. Then he performed the Tawaaf of the Women (Tawaaf al-Nisa) and did not pray the two cycles until he remembered it at Al-Abtah, so he prayed four cycles. He (peace be upon him) said: 'He should return and pray four cycles at the Standing Place (of Ibrahim).'

key_terms.طَوَافَ النِّسَاءِ: The Circumambulation of the Women (Tawaaf al-Nisa)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if one forgets to pray the two cycles after Tawaaf and Sa'i and remembers later?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the specific location-based obligation of the two rak'ahs following Tawaaf, emphasizing that the prayer is intrinsically linked to the Maqam Ibrahim. It addresses a scenario where a pilgrim delays the prayer until after Sa'i and the Tawaaf al-Nisa', requiring a return to the Maqam to fulfill the missed four cycles, thereby reinforcing the jurisprudential principle that the prayer's validity is tied to its designated spot rather than just the act of Tawaaf itself. This ruling highlights the precision of Shia fiqh in maintaining ritual integrity even when actions are performed out of the ideal sequence.
